result.title: LINDA: Low Resource Foot Ulcer Segmentation using Local Similarity and Iterative Neural Dynamics
result.summary: Foot ulcers are a leading cause of lower limb amputation, and the highest burden often falls on low and middle income regions where specialists and computing hardware are both scarce. Wound monitoring tools are most useful there when they are accurate yet small enough to run on ordinary devices, but accuracy usually comes from heavy networks. We present LINDA, a compact model that grounds segmentation in an explicit structural prior instead of raw intensity. A Local Self-Similarity (LSS) map, computed directly from the image and stable under local lighting changes, is fused into a ResNet-34 encoder, and a small Liquid Time-Constant module refines the boundary over four iterative steps. With every model trained under one protocol on the FUSeg 2021 dataset, LINDA obtains the best Dice (86.68\%), IoU (79.67\%), and boundary accuracy (HD95 6.37 pixels) in our comparison while using only 25.70M parameters, fewer than the U-Net and transformer baselines. As the LSS map is a fixed function of the input, it exposes the structural cues the model follows in a readable form. Together this makes LINDA an accurate, inspectable, and lightweight option for wound assessment in resource-constrained care.

AI.brief_summary: LINDA 提出一个轻量足部溃疡分割模型：将图像自身的局部自相似（LSS）图作为结构先验融入 ResNet-34 编码器，并用小型 Liquid Time-Constant 模块做四步迭代边界精修，在 FUSeg 2021 上以约 25.7M 参数取得最优 Dice 与边界精度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其液态时间常数模块在固定四步内迭代更新分割状态、以及固定函数式 LSS 旁路提供可读结构线索，可供核查 LVR 中循环状态更新与视觉证据注入的可解释性，但论文本身不涉及多模态推理。
